## Demo 1 — the phantom regression

A team's eval pass rate falls over two weeks. Their dashboard flags a regression and the
on-call engineer starts bisecting.

**Ground truth: the provider rotated the judge snapshot behind a stable model string. The
system under test was byte-identical throughout, and the rollback would have been pure
waste.**

```text
$ benchlock verdict
verdict=judge          confidence: anytime-valid at alpha=0.05
  E_anchor    =    17222.4   (threshold 40.0, crossed at run 34)
  E_system    =    58382.5   (threshold 40.0, crossed at run 29)
  E_corrected =        0.5   (threshold 40.0; the system move with the judge's removed)

- the anchor set moved -0.088 [CS: -0.155, -0.020]
- the system under test does not touch the anchor set; only the judge can move it
- your system moved -0.092 raw; anchor-corrected +0.001 [CS: -0.067, +0.069]
- anchor provisioning: ADEQUATE
  minimum detectable judge shift at this anchor size = 0.032, over 55 monitored run(s) of 200
  anchor items
- judge: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (config unchanged all epoch)

DO NOT roll back. Re-baseline against the judge's current behaviour:
  benchlock rebaseline --reason judge-version-change
```

`benchlock gate` exits **0**. A judge change must not fail your build.

## Demo 2 — the real regression, correctly named

The same pipeline. This time the system genuinely regressed, and the judge did not move.

**Ground truth: a system regression, with the judge held constant.**

```text
$ benchlock verdict
verdict=system         confidence: anytime-valid at alpha=0.05
  E_anchor    =        0.5   (threshold 40.0, not crossed)
  E_system    =   148208.9   (threshold 40.0, crossed at run 27)
  E_corrected =     6678.3   (threshold 40.0; the system move with the judge's removed)

- the anchor set is stable: +0.001 [CS: -0.063, +0.065]
- your system moved -0.038 [CS: -0.107, +0.031]
- the anchor set could have detected a judge shift as small as 0.032, which is smaller than the
  observed move, so the judge is ruled out

CI gate: FAIL (exit 1)
  benchlock report
```

## Demo 3 — the honest one, which is the point of the project

The same real regression as Demo 2, from the same seed — but the anchor set was configured
at 40 items instead of the 200 that `benchlock plan` asked for.

Most tools would say "regression" here and be right by luck. Benchlock refuses, says why,
and says exactly what to change.

**A tool that is confidently wrong one time in ten is worse than useless in a CI gate,
because people learn to ignore it.**

```text
$ benchlock verdict
verdict=indeterminate  confidence: anytime-valid at alpha=0.05
  E_anchor    =        0.5   (threshold 40.0, not crossed)
  E_system    =    99145.9   (threshold 40.0, crossed at run 28)
  E_corrected =        8.1   (threshold 40.0; the system move with the judge's removed)

- your system score moved, and the anchor set did not
- BUT the anchor set is under-provisioned: at n=40 the minimum judge shift this anchor process
  could have detected by run 55 is 0.044. The observed system move is 0.038. A judge shift of that
  size would be INVISIBLE here
- benchlock will not attribute this to your system. It cannot rule out the judge
- anchor provisioning: UNDER_PROVISIONED
  at n=40 the smallest judge shift detectable by run 55 is 0.044
- judge: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (config unchanged all epoch)

Fix the provisioning, then this becomes decidable:
  benchlock plan --target-shift 0.05
```

`benchlock gate` exits **2** — a warning, not a failure, and not a verdict.
